newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. BANK SETTLES RACE DISCRIMINATION ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. BANK SETTLES RACE DISCRIMINATION ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: A New York bank will make $55 million in low-interest mortgage loans in communities with large minority populations to settle allegations that it had an explicit policy of avoiding those areas, the Justice Department said Wednesday.

Albank Financial Institution and Albank FSB and the Justice Department reached the agreement, to be filed in U.S. District Court in Albany, N.Y., to resolve allegations that the bank violated the Fair Housing Act and the Equal Credit Opportunity Act.
Albank, a federally chartered savings bank with $3.5 billion in assets based in Albany, denied the charges but agreed to resolve the case through a settlement.

"We first began looking at Albank's lending practices earlier this year," Attorney General Janet Reno told reporters. "What we found was that Albank carved out areas of the map where they chose not to make loans, areas that were minority enclaves."
Albank seldom made loans in those areas, the investigation found, and when it did make exceptions and lend there, the borrowers were almost always white.

The enclaves included minority sections of Westchester County, N.Y., and seven Connecticut cities including Hartford, New Haven and Stamford, where blacks and Hispanics made up 25 percent or more of the population.

Paul Hancock, a senior civil rights official at Justice, said the bank's "explicit" written policy outlining lending practices in minorities communities was "somewhat unusual" and that the $55 million settlement was fairly large for this kind of case.

Under the agreement, which Hancock said would involve about $9 million in out-of-pocket expenses for the bank, the bank will provide $55 million over the next five years in mortgage loans at 1.5 percent below the going market rate .
"We aren't asking you (banks) to make bad loans," Reno said. "But don't decide what you will do based on race or some other inappropriate classification."
